code: run_one <- function(seed, ve_floor) {   sc  <- hermes$simulate_waning_scenario(ve_floor = ve_floor, rng_seed = seed)   sim <- list(demographic = sc$demographic_data, vaccination = sc$vaccination_data,               incidence = sc$incidence_data_reduced, params = sc$params,               study_end = sc$study_end)   pop  <- ve_population(sim)   prev <- daily_prevalence(daily_incidence(pop))   foi  <- force_of_infection(prev, age_group_sizes(pop))   cp   <- counting_process(pop, censor_at_vaccination =                              reported_soon_after_vaccination(pop, 7))   sd   <- make_stan_data(expand_person_days(cp), foi)   ve   <- extract_ve(fit_ve(sd, seed = seed, refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE))   ve$truth <- true_ve(ve$days_since_vax, sim$params)   ve$seed  <- seed   ve } # about 20 s simulation + 40 s fit per replicate

Method developed (workshop repository, branch group-D): data_wrangling.R: merge data, sample cohort 10,000, daily incidence age group vaccination status, counting-process data split vaccination, expansion person-days, prevalence reported cases (7-day infectious period starting 2 days reporting). prepare_stan_data.R: age-structured FoI ‾(tc,)=∑′Ca′aIa′eff(tc−1)/Na\bar (t_c, ) = \sum_{'} C_{'} ^{\text{eff}}_{'}(t_c - 1) / N_a using POLYMOD Netherlands contact matrix, plus overall-prevalence version; person-days aggregated cells. model.stan: Poisson approximation Cox model, log⁡μ=log⁡β+log⁡‾+log⁡D+γ(t)V\log\mu = \log\beta + \log\bar + \log D + \gamma(t)V, daily random walk γ(t)\gamma(t) γ(1)∼N(−1,1)\gamma(1) \sim N(-1, 1). run_model.R: fits age-structured overall-prevalence versions. analysis_Poisson_and_Cox.R (Hein Putter, 2026-06-19): frequentist Poisson Cox fits piecewise-constant hazard ratios. title: Get started
text: ve_population() joins demographic, vaccination case data one row per person. epidemic peaks vaccination coverage still rising. waning scenario, cases among vaccinated people continue end study protection fades.
code: pops <- lapply(scenarios, ve_population)  daily <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pops), function(s) {   p <- pops[[s]]   cases <- p[p$infected & p$time_of_reporting <= 180, ]   vax_at_report <- cases$vaccinated & cases$time_of_vaccination < cases$time_of_reporting   tab <- as.data.frame(table(day = cases$time_of_reporting,                              status = ifelse(vax_at_report, "Vaccinated", "Unvaccinated")))   tab$day <- as.numeric(as.character(tab$day))   tab$scenario <- s   tab })) coverage <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pops), function(s) {   v <- pops[[s]]$time_of_vaccination   data.frame(scenario = s, day = 0:180,              coverage = sapply(0:180, function(d) mean(!is.na(v) & v <= d))) })) scale_k <- max(tapply(daily$Freq, list(daily$day, daily$scenario), sum), na.rm = TRUE)  ggplot() +   geom_col(data = daily, aes(day, Freq, fill = status), width = 1) +   geom_step(data = coverage, aes(day, coverage * scale_k), colour = "grey20") +   facet_wrap(~ factor(scenario, levels = names(scenarios)), ncol = 1) +   scale_fill_manual(values = c(Unvaccinated = "grey65", Vaccinated = "#d95f02")) +   scale_y_continuous("Reported cases per day",                      sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / scale_k, name = "Vaccination coverage (line)",                                          labels = scales::percent)) +   labs(x = "Study day", fill = NULL) +   theme(legend.position = "top")

title: Get started
text: model Poisson approximation Cox model. log hazard ratio vaccination, γ(t)\gamma(t), follows random walk days since vaccination, VE(t) = 1 − exp(γ(t)\gamma(t)): log⁡μ=log⁡β+log⁡‾(tc,)+log⁡(person-days)+γ(t)V. \log \mu = \log\beta + \log \bar (t_c, ) + \log(\text{person-days}) + \gamma(t)\,V. Fitting needs cmdstanr CmdStan: vignette can built without CmdStan, results loaded fits run advance exactly analysis scenarios (data-raw/ve_fits.R).
code: fit <- fit_ve(sd, seed = 42) ve <- extract_ve(fit) expected <- expected_cases(fit, sd, by = c("day", "vax_status")) fits <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "ve_fits.rds", package = "surviver")) # convergence diagnostics and key parameters of each fit round(sapply(fits[c("waning", "no_waning")], function(f) unlist(f$diagnostics)), 3) #>             waning no_waning #> max_rhat     1.004     1.003 #> divergences  0.000     0.000 #> log_beta    -4.508    -4.482 #> sigma_gamma  0.149     0.251

title: Estimate Time-Varying Vaccine Effectiveness
text: surviver estimates vaccine effectiveness function time since vaccination, VE(t), individual-level data vaccination reported infections. person’s hazard infection driven force infection exposed , built reported cases age-structured contact matrix. Vaccination multiplies hazard exp(γ(t)), γ(t) varies time since vaccination: log⁡h=log⁡β+log⁡‾(tc,)+γ(t)V,VE(t)=1−eγ(t) \log h = \log\beta + \log \bar (t_c, ) + \gamma(t)\,V, \qquad \mathrm{VE}(t) = 1 - e^{\gamma(t)} model Poisson approximation Cox model, fitted Stan random-walk prior γ(t), VE can rise, plateau wane without assuming functional form. Status: experimental. See lab notebook checked open issues.

title: Estimate Time-Varying Vaccine Effectiveness
text: Estimate VE(t) simulated dataset true VE known: Get started vignette shows epidemic dynamics model fit cases. use data, pass ve_population() folder containing demographic_data.rds, vaccination_data.rds incidence_data_reduced.rds, list demographic, vaccination incidence data frames (see ?ve_population).
code: library(surviver)  # person-level data: demographics, vaccination and reported cases pop <- ve_population(ve_sim_waning)  # force of infection by day and age group, from reported cases inc  <- daily_incidence(pop) prev <- daily_prevalence(inc, duration_infection = 7, reporting_delay = 2) foi  <- force_of_infection(prev, age_group_sizes(pop), contact_matrix = polymod_nl)  # person-days split at vaccination, aggregated for Stan. People reported # within 7 days of vaccination are censored at vaccination (probably # infected before it) early <- reported_soon_after_vaccination(pop, window = 7) pd <- expand_person_days(counting_process(pop, censor_at_vaccination = early)) sd <- make_stan_data(pd, foi)  # fit and plot against the true curve (VE is not estimable for the first # 7 days after vaccination once early cases are censored) fit <- fit_ve(sd, seed = 42) ve  <- extract_ve(fit) plot_ve(ve[ve$days_since_vax > 7, ], truth = ve_sim_waning$params)

title: surviver 0.0.0.9000
text: Initial package, consolidating Group D analysis Lorentz Center workshop (June 2026). Data preparation: ve_population(), sample_cohort(), daily_incidence(), daily_prevalence(), counting_process(), expand_person_days(). Exposure: force_of_infection() (age-structured overall), age_group_sizes(), contact_matrix_hermes(). Model: make_stan_data(), fit_ve() non-centred (default) centred Stan models, extract_ve(), plot_ve(). counting_process(censor_at_vaccination = ) reported_soon_after_vaccination() censor people infected vaccination reported . expected_cases() compares observed model-expected case counts. Validation helpers: true_ve(), simulate_counts(). Datasets: ve_sim_waning, ve_sim_no_waning (HERMES simulations known VE(t)) polymod_nl. “Get started” vignette figures epidemic dynamics, model fit VE estimates (fits precomputed inst/extdata/ve_fits.rds). Lab notebook article recording development validation checks.
